candidates.expected_effect: Remove unreachable OTP, library, and fixture modules while preserving the exact BH-01 proof inventory.
candidates.tradeoff: Requires a trustworthy module-reachability model and can produce false-small bundles if dynamic calls are missed.
candidates.browser_constraints: Must remain compatible with AtomVM/Popcorn loading and the same manifest/integrity contract.
candidates.repeat_requirement: Produce separate before/after manifests and rerun Phases 3 through 9; no estimate receives budget credit.
candidates.review_trigger: Before any release claim and when the bundle builder gains reachability pruning.

candidates.expected_effect: Serve precompressed content-addressed artifacts with correct negotiation, MIME, integrity, cache, and isolation headers.
candidates.tradeoff: Adds deployment variants and requires CDN/proxy validation; local compression alone proves no network saving.
candidates.browser_constraints: Must preserve streaming Wasm behavior and never serve compressed bytes without correct Content-Encoding and Vary semantics.
candidates.repeat_requirement: Capture before/after network bytes and startup distributions in Chrome and Firefox, then repeat external qualification when available.

candidates.target: application AVM and future optional packages
candidates.expected_effect: Separate required startup modules from future optional families only where AtomVM loading semantics permit deterministic lazy reachability.
candidates.tradeoff: Additional requests and lifecycle states may worsen startup or reliability and must not hide mandatory fixture code.
candidates.browser_constraints: No service-worker dependency or browser-only component semantics may enter portable packages.
candidates.repeat_requirement: Measure one exact before/after candidate after pruning, including cold/warm/offline/failure paths.
candidates.review_trigger: After the application reachability experiment establishes a truthful ownership boundary.

candidates.owner: browser host and DOM renderer owners

baseline.evidence: local interaction and DOM distributions in the desktop summary

candidates.expected_effect: Potentially reduce bridge calls only if a future representative component trace demonstrates pressure.
candidates.tradeoff: Batching can increase latency, obscure ordering, and complicate cancellation and stale-generation semantics.
candidates.browser_constraints: Must preserve the bounded closed protocol and deterministic normalized trace.
candidates.repeat_requirement: No implementation until a traced bottleneck exists; then retain before/after trace and timing evidence.
candidates.review_trigger: A future representative trace exceeds its interaction budget with bridge overhead attribution.

rejected_approaches.approach: Remove required difficult scenarios or artifacts from the measured profile
rejected_approaches.reason: This would invalidate the BH-01 proof inventory and create a false-small candidate.

rejected_approaches.approach: Move Elixir component behavior or presentation decisions into JavaScript or the Phoenix server
rejected_approaches.reason: This violates the host-neutral semantic and authority boundaries.

rejected_approaches.approach: Lower thresholds, change metric boundaries, or reduce sample counts after seeing results
rejected_approaches.reason: Quality-contract changes require separate versioned review and cannot retroactively manufacture a pass.

rejected_approaches.approach: Treat desktop emulation or Linux engine builds as mobile, Safari, Windows, or accessibility qualification
rejected_approaches.reason: Those obligations are explicitly deferred and non-substitutable.

recommendation.active_development: continue conditionally while the unpruned application AVM remains an explicit feasibility risk
recommendation.required_follow_up: Run reachability pruning and actual Brotli serving as separately reviewed before/after experiments before release qualification.
recommendation.support_effect: none; these candidates and observations grant no browser, mobile, accessibility, production, or release support
